title: FedDefender: Client-Side Attack-Tolerant Federated Learning

problem.claim: Federated learning is vulnerable to model poisoning attacks in which malicious clients interfere with training.

gap.claim: Server-side defenses based on careful model aggregation may be ineffective under non-identically distributed data or when attackers can access benign clients' information.

contributions.claim: FedDefender is a client-side defense mechanism designed to help benign clients train robust local models and reduce the adverse impact of malicious model updates.
The method combines attack-tolerant local meta update with attack-tolerant global knowledge distillation.
The client-side defense has a flexible structure and can work with existing server-side strategies.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Evaluations in real-world scenarios across multiple datasets show improved robustness against model poisoning attacks.

narrative_sequence.summary: Federated learning supports decentralized learning while preserving privacy.
Malicious clients can poison models, and server-side aggregation defenses may fail under heterogeneous data or attacker access to benign-client information.
FedDefender introduces a client-side defense with attack-tolerant local meta update and global knowledge distillation.
The components seek noise-resilient parameters while extracting knowledge from a potentially corrupted global model.
The authors report improved robustness in evaluations across multiple datasets and real-world scenarios.

source_observation.claim: A client-side defense is intended to remain useful even when server-side defenses cannot identify or remove adversaries.

interpretation.claim: Defense mechanisms placed at different points in a distributed training pipeline can provide complementary protection when one point has limited visibility.

application.claim: Consider combining client-side robustness mechanisms with existing server-side aggregation defenses in federated learning deployments.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish effectiveness across specific attack types, data distributions, or deployment conditions.

unknowns: Specific model poisoning attack types and threat assumptions are not described.
Datasets, baselines, metrics, quantitative results, and evaluation details are not provided.
